title: ROCm/hrx-system low-latency HIP runtime, direct HSA/PM4 dispatch, and Loom JIT compiler substrate
observations: HRX System is a clean-slate runtime and compiler infrastructure providing an alternative implementation of HIP within ROCm, designed by IREE/Nod.ai maintainers for low-latency, high-performance integration with AMD GPUs, NPUs, and CPUs.

Bypasses the multi-layer legacy ROCm stack (hip-runtime, comgr, rocprofiler) by implementing direct HSA/KFD execution with user-space AQL packet queues and direct PM4 command processor packet emission.

Provides a drop-in binary replacement libamdhip64.so (24,764 lines in binding/hip/api.c) that accelerates existing HIP applications (vLLM, llama.cpp, PyTorch) via LD_PRELOAD with zero code modifications.

Introduces Loom: a source-first native compiler substrate with a public C API (loomc) that compiles async device kernels and model programs directly to native HSACO ELF64 objects in under 2ms without runtime LLVM/clang subprocess overhead.
Loom features comprehensive matrix contracts for AMDGPU (MFMA on CDNA3/gfx942, WMMA on RDNA3.5/gfx1151 and RDNA4/gfx1201, SMFMAC/SWMMAC sparse variants, scaled F8/F6/F4 micro-quantization).

Implements KPACK (common/kpack.c): a compressed kernel package format with MessagePack TOCs, zstd decompression, and subsettable AMDGPU target ID expansion (sramecc, xnack) for compact multi-architecture kernel distribution.

Includes a stream-ordered VMM slab allocator (vmm_slab_provider.c) that pairs large virtual address reservations with lazy physical page commits, preventing VRAM address fragmentation during dynamic batching.
Co-designs kernel correctness policy and benchmark workloads in source IR via check.case and check.benchmark operations, supporting parameter sweeps and assignment dictionaries.
Features compile reports (loom-compile-report) with exact structural LDS bank-conflict service models and scheduled vs final VGPR pressure analysis, enabling pre-silicon tile optimization.
Integrates an asynchronous device event bus with in-band GPU AddressSanitizer (ASAN) fault reporting, capturing exact faulting addresses, workgroup/workitem IDs, and shadow memory state.

candidates.outcome: Filed #11094 to implement native AMDGPU ELF64/HSACO emitter in internal/compute without runtime LLVM.

candidates.effect: KPACK compressed multi-target kernel package parser and dynamic architecture resolver.
candidates.outcome: Filed #11095 to add pure-Go KPACK container reader and target fallback resolver.

candidates.effect: Stream-ordered VMM slab allocator with virtual address reservation and lazy physical memory commit.

candidates.effect: In-IR test oracle and benchmark parameter specification with assignment dictionaries.
candidates.outcome: Filed #11098 to unify kernel numeric verification oracles and benchmark parameter sweeps.

candidates.effect: Asynchronous device event bus for in-band GPU kernel AddressSanitizer (ASAN) fault attribution.
candidates.outcome: Filed #11097 to add device event sink and in-band GPU kernel memory defect reporting.

candidates.effect: Transparent HIP runtime drop-in shim with stream batch memory operations for low-latency kernel dispatch.
candidates.outcome: Watch for potential LD_PRELOAD interposition when benchmarking third-party ROCm/HIP engines without relinking.

candidates.effect: Compile-time LDS/shared-memory bank conflict and VGPR pressure diagnostic modeling.
candidates.outcome: Watch as an offline heuristic model to reject suboptimal kernel tile shapes prior to hardware benchmarking.
